ideas.title: Ten Minutes Under
ideas.premise: Eli takes a sunset shortcut past a creek mouth on a frozen Minnesota lake, falls through six-centimeter ice, and has one minute to breathe, ten to get out and an hour before he passes out.
ideas.hook: When the ice broke under me, I had ten minutes. Not seconds.
ideas.twist: Most people think they have seconds and panic, or tear off the heavy jacket; the 1-10-1 rule says you have time, and the jacket's trapped air holds you up.
ideas.world: Side view at sunset sliding to blue hour, cross-section for the six centimeters and the trapped air, top map for 'turn back the way you came', brother's red shack for the cliffhanger.
ideas.fact: Minnesota DNR: stay off new clear ice under 10 cm; white ice is about half as strong. Cold-water experts teach 1-10-1.
ideas.verify: DNR thickness table wording; 1-10-1 numbers as approximate.

ideas.title: Never Rush the Hole
ideas.premise: Eli's brother sees him go through the ice from his shack sixty meters away and has to decide in seconds how to help without becoming the second person in the water.
ideas.hook: My brother ran straight at the hole. That's how two people drown.
ideas.twist: Reach, throw, don't go: lie flat and pass a rod or rope from the strong ice instead of running to the edge.
ideas.world: Night side view with the lit shack, top map with the brother's path and a red dashed 'wrong' route, cut view of the ice edge breaking under the runner.
ideas.fact: US Coast Guard and Red Cross ice-rescue guidance: reach, throw, don't go.
ideas.verify: Exact wording of the reach-throw-go guidance.

ideas.title: The Color of Ice
ideas.premise: Eli has to cross the lake back to the shack before dark and the only clue to which ice will hold him is its color.
ideas.hook: Clear ice held me. The white ice right next to it didn't.
ideas.twist: White, snowy ice looks solid but is roughly half as strong as clear blue ice of the same thickness.
ideas.world: Side view at dusk with patches of different ice, cross-section with the thickness ruler, swatch chips naming each color.
ideas.fact: Minnesota DNR: white ice is about half as strong as new clear ice.

ideas.title: Sixty Meters of Dark
ideas.premise: After he gets out, soaked Eli still has sixty meters of open ice and a falling temperature between him and the warm shack.
ideas.hook: Getting out of the water was only half of it.
ideas.twist: Keep moving to shelter and get dry and warm; don't stop to rest on the ice.
ideas.world: Blue hour to night side view, top map distance pill counting down to the shack, freeze-frame on the mistake of sitting down.
ideas.fact: CDC hypothermia guidance: get to a warm place, remove wet clothing, warm the core first.

ideas.title: Creek Mouth
ideas.premise: A shortcut past the creek mouth saves Eli three minutes on the walk home and puts him over the thinnest ice on the lake.
ideas.hook: The shortcut saved me three minutes. It cost me the ice.
ideas.twist: Moving water under the ice keeps it thin even in a deep freeze; inlets and outlets are the most dangerous spots.
ideas.world: Side view of the creek channel, cut view of current eroding the slab from below, top map of the safe route around.
ideas.fact: State DNRs warn that ice near inlets, outlets and moving water is thinner.
ideas.verify: DNR guidance on inlets and currents.
